mūlaśodhana
------------------------------------------
Cleansing the body is an important aspect of हठयोग. Such processes are known by the term ‘ṣaṭkarma’, one of which is धौति. Of the four kinds of धौति, मूलशोधन is also one. It is the purification of the rectum and the large intestines using a stalk of the root of turmeric or the middle finger of the hand. It should be done only under the guidance of an expert.
See also DHAUTI and ŚAṬKARMAS.

Mūlar
------------------------------------------
Also known as तिरुमूलर् Nāyanār (tiru = Śrī; nāyanār = a Śaiva saint in general), मूलर् is one of the 64 Śaiva saints of Tamil Nadu, who probably lived in the 6th century A. D.
He was one of the eight disciples of a great teacher Tirumandi Devar.
It seems he was living on a hillock called Potiyān. Once he strongly felt to see the sage अगस्त्य and came to the southern country, visiting many a शिव temple on the way. In one village, on the bank of Kāveri he found a herd of cows shedding tears. He came to know that the cowherd named Mūlan had just died. Out of pity for the cows, he, using his special yogic power known as ‘parakāyapraveśa’ (entering into the dead-body of another person), entered into Mūlan’s body, but kept his own body safely hidden in the cavity of a huge tree.
The villagers found this ‘Mūlan’ diffe-rent from the old Mūlan, discovered that he had become a saint (Tirumūlar) and let him go freely as he liked.
This तिरुमूलर् later found that his original body had disappeared! Hence he was forced to live in his new body.
He often used to go into समाधि and compose his work Tirumandiram (of 3000 verses) whenever he came down to normal चोन्स्चिओउस्नेस्स्.
See also NĀYANMĀRS.

Mūlaveda
------------------------------------------
The Pāñcarātra Āgamas, the basic texts of वैष्णविस्म् or the भागवत Cult were called ‘Mūlaveda’ by their followers since they were taught by God नारायण Himself to the sages नर, शाण्डिल्य, प्रह्लाद and others.
See also PĀÑCARĀTRA ĀGAMAS.

mūlāvidyā
(‘universal or primeval इग्नोरन्चे or nescience’)
------------------------------------------
Some of the schools of Advaita Vedānta categorise अविद्या or nescience into two types: मूल-अविद्या (universal or primeval nescience) and tula-अविद्या (individual nescience).
The former is the material cause of this world.
The latter is the अविद्या that covers चोन्स्चिओउस्नेस्स् circumscribed by particular objects, like the body.
Whether मूलाविद्या is located in ब्रह्मन् or in the जीव has been a moot point. The Vivaraṇa school of Pañcapādikā holds the former view whereas the Bhāmatī school sticks to the latter.
See also ADVAITA VEDĀNTA DARŚANA.

Mūla
------------------------------------------
Hindu अस्त्रोनोम्य् lists 28 nakṣatras or groups of स्तर्स्. The मूल is the 19th in the list. It comprises two stars—the lambda and the upsilon Scorpio. It is generally considered as inauspicious.
The Atharvaveda calls it as ‘Vicṛtan’.
See also NAKṢATRAS.
